answer: Sybil resistance comes from a per-identity capital lock that cannot be split. An agent must post a bond before earning; running N fake identities requires N separate bonds, each time-delayed past the epoch and released only to the identity that staked it. An attacker inflating accounts pays the full stake every time while gaining no extra payout, so the cost scales linearly or worse. Reputation stays a clear prism, each record costly to fabricate, and fake swarms blow away like a gale over empty dune sand.
